rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The energy in a capacitor is (1/2) C V^2, which is also Q^2/(2C) and (1/2) Q V. The one half is the average of a voltage that grows from zero to V. The battery supplies twice this energy, and the other half becomes heat. The stored energy resides in the electric field.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
C = Q/V
C = ε₀A/d
U = ½CV²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Average voltage during charging is V/2.  ·  Energy density is (1/2) ε0 E^2.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Charging a capacitor means moving charge from one plate to the other against a rising potential difference. The work done is the energy stored.  ·  At an intermediate charge q the voltage is q/C, so the next bit of charge dq costs (q/C) dq. Integrating from 0 to Q gives U = Q^2 / (2C). With Q = C V this is also (1/2) C V^2 and (1/2) Q V.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Stored energy  ·  Average voltage  ·  Battery work  ·  Field energy

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Energy is the work of charging.  ·  The factor 1/2 is the average voltage.  ·  The battery supplies twice the stored energy.  ·  The energy sits in the field.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Capacitance C = Q/V; parallel-plate C = ε₀A/d (larger with dielectric: C = ε₀εᵣA/d).  ·  Energy stored U = ½CV² = Q²/2C.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: How much of the battery's energy is stored?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A 5.0 μF capacitor is charged to 200 V by a battery. Find the stored energy and the energy supplied by the battery.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Stored energy is → B  ·  The battery supplies → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The factor one half appears because the voltage starts at zero and ends at V. The average voltage during charging is V/2, and charge Q times that average is (1/2) Q V.  ·  A battery at constant V supplies energy Q V, which is C V^2. The capacitor stores only half of that. The other half is dissipated as heat in the resistance of the connecting wires during the charging current.  ·  The stored energy can be written as a density in the field, (1/2) ε0 E^2 in vacuum. The energy is between the plates, in the field, not inside the metal of the plates.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ capacitance c = q/v; parallel-plate c = ε₀a/d (larger with dielectric: c = ε₀εᵣa/d)..  ·  The battery energy is not all stored.  ·  The one-half is required.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Energy is in the field, not in the metal.  ·  Fixed Q and fixed V change the energy in opposite ways when C changes.  ·  Say whether Q or V is held constant.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The missing half is heat, not a second capacitor.  ·  Write U = (1/2) C V^2 and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  Series: 1/C = Σ1/C (same Q); Parallel: C = ΣC (same V).  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: capacitance c = q/v; parallel-plate c = ε₀a/d (larger with dielectric: c = ε₀εᵣa/d).  ·  If an isolated capacitor has its plates pulled apart, Q is fixed, C falls and the stored energy rises.
